r: Most under the Ikshvakus – queens, princesses and rich lay women funded stupas and viharas; kings were not the chief patrons
Served Buddhism in the reign of **Virapurushadatta** (her Chula-Dhammagiri record is dated in his **14th** regnal year)
A Nagarjunakonda sculpture shows **Mathariputra Virapurushadatta** trampling a Shivalinga – a sign of his turn to Buddhism
Vedic: Ashvamedha, Rajasuya, Vajapeya, Agnistoma; worshipped **Virupakshapati** (Shiva) and **Mahasena** (Skanda); agraharas to northern Brahmins

**Only** Ikshvaku king to adopt Buddhism (earlier Vedic; did not wholly drop Brahmanical ties); "**Ashoka of the South**", **Sri Parvatadhipati**; rebuilt the Maha Chaitya under Acharya **Bhadanta Ananda**; set up the **Sriparvata University**
Revived Brahmanism; first Hindu temples; first Sanskrit inscriptions; still built a vihara for the **Bahushrutiyas** in his mother's name
Vedic; deity Mahasena; custom of **chhaya-stambhas** (shadow pillars) near graves began

0.x: **Puranic Shaivism, Vaishnavism and Shakti worship** all thrived; the Ikshvakus were the **last royal Buddhist zenith** in Andhra.

r: **Tutelary deity** of the **Ikshvakus** of Vijayapuri – protector of **children**; women offered bangles for progeny
Its installation = beginning of **Shakti worship**; Hariti was also a mother goddess of the Early Chalukyas
Salankayana **Nandivarman II** – land grant in the Pedavegi inscription
Purvasailiya, Aparasailiya, Bahushrutiya, Rajagirika, Siddharthika (the Mahaviharavasin is Theravada)
Knew the **Digha and Majjhima Nikayas** by heart
A **Dhatugarbha** stupa over the Buddha's bodily relics: "**Samma Sambudhasa dhatuvara parigahita**"
Built by **Yajnasri Satakarni** for **Acharya Nagarjuna**; rebuilt by **Chamtisri** with **9 ayaka pillars**
Stone mandapa at the eastern gateway of the Maha Chaitya at **Kantakasala (Ghantasala)**; **seven viharas at Papili**
Lands that received the Dhamma (Bodhisri's inscription)
**Kashmir, Gandhara, China, Chilata, Tosali, Aparanta, Vanga, Vanavasi, Yavana, Damila, Palura**
Took Buddhism from the **Pallava-bhoga** region to Sri Lanka (Mahavamsa)
The Chinese pilgrim **Itsing** (I-tsing, in India **671–695** CE) saw Indian students memorising Nagarjuna's *Suhrllekha*, a letter to **Yajnasri Satakarni**
**India's first structural Hindu temples** – **9** Shaiva + **1** Vaishnava at Nagarjunakonda
**Harati, Mahajana, Kumara Swami, Pushpabhadra Swami, Ashtabhuja Narayana Swami**; also Nandikeshwara and Navagraha
Started by **Virapurushadatta**, completed by **Ehuvala Santamula**; Shiva; **Gajaprishtha** (elephant-back) plan
Commander **Elisiri** (of Ehuvala); for **Kumara Swami (Kartikeya)**; Sanskrit record
**Shivasena**, commander of the Abhira king **Vasusena**; **first Vaishnava temple** in Andhra

3.x: Inscriptions of Vasishthiputra Santamula were found at **Rentala** and Kesanapalli near Nagarjunakonda.

r: **Nagarjunakonda / Vijayapuri**, named after him; "**Dakshina Gaya**", sacred to **Mahayana** (**Bodh Gaya** is sacred to **Hinayana**)
Built viharas and chaityas at Sriparvata for him
Identified by **N. Venkataramanayya**; different from **Sriparvataswami**, the Vishnukundin family deity (Srisaila Mallikarjuna)
Miss World contestants visited **Buddhavanam** next to Nagarjunakonda (Buddhist circuit)
